llvmorg-17.0.6.reviewed_interpretation: The local unique_ptr destroys the input MemoryBuffer on both normal success and normal failure returns.

llvmorg-23.1.4.reviewed_interpretation: The local unique_ptr destroys the input MemoryBuffer on both normal success and normal failure returns.

new_nonconsuming_API.reviewed_interpretation: The new function parses through the caller-owned buffer; do not swap to this API without changing the Rust ownership contract.

method.retrieval: GitHub connector fetch_file with exact tag and path; full UTF-8 source preserved and matched to returned Git blob SHA.
method.declaration_comparison: Remove comments, preprocessor lines, LLVM_C_ABI visibility and extern-C marker macros; compare C declaration lexical tokens, including parameter names and pointer types.
method.macro_check: Require each of the five exact target-initializer macro declaration patterns in both versions; X86 availability/export still requires actual toolchain validation.
method.enum_check: Evaluate explicit integer constants and subsequent implicit increments for the selected enums; reject unsupported numeric syntax.
method.ownership_check: Match the unique_ptr owner in both exact source definitions and retain the full bodies for human review; this is not a general C++ ownership proof.

limitations: No candidate production edits were reviewed in this receipt.
No builds, linked-symbol export checks, C ABI execution, sanitizers, native tests, or performance measurements were run.
Matching declarations do not prove all transitive typedef ABI or runtime semantics unchanged.
No preprocessor or C compiler was invoked by this source inventory script.
Source hashes verify byte identity with GitHub-reported blobs, not a separate release-signature verification.
The LLVM23 pipeline, target-machine implementation, ABI lowering, and generated-code quality still require exact-toolchain regression and measurement.
